- When sentiment is consistently neutral or negative (≤ 0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak or use 2-period moving average.
- If sentiment shows early positive signals (e.g., 0.33 or higher), model frequently overreacts; dampen forecast by 1–2% for 2–3 periods ahead.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- If sentiment is negative and price is trending up, model often fails to recognize reversal; reduce forecast slope by 50% if sentiment turns negative within 3 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extrapolating from 18-day history; use 30-day moving average or weighted average (more weight on recent 7 days) to reduce lag bias.
